blocks.body: Present Perfect: Forms and Use — have / has + V3 for present results, life experience, recent actions, and situations or periods continuing up to now.

{"level":"A2–B1","intro":"In Present Perfect, we use have / has + V3 when we describe an earlier action or state connected with the present moment.","rules":[{"label":"have / has + V3","color":"emerald","text":"This is the basic affirmative pattern. V3 is the past participle, or third form, of the verb.","example":"I have finished. / She has cleaned the kitchen."},{"label":"No finished past-time expression","color":"blue","text":"Do not use Present Perfect with a finished-time expression such as yesterday or last year. An exact starting point with since is possible.","example":"We have lived here since 2021. / I saw him yesterday."},{"label":"Connection with the present","color":"amber","text":"The important point is not the past fact itself, but the result, experience, or period up to now.","example":"I have lost my keys. / They have lived here since 2021."}]}

{"title":"1. Basic formula","intro":"V3 is the past participle, or third form, of the verb. Have / has is an auxiliary here and does not separately mean possession.","items":[{"label":"I / You / We / They","title":"have + V3","subtitle":"I have finished. / They have arrived. Contractions: I've, you've, we've, they've."},{"label":"He / She / It","title":"has + V3","subtitle":"She has started. / It has stopped. Contractions: he's, she's, it's."},{"label":"Regular verbs","title":"work → worked; finish → finished","subtitle":"With regular verbs, V3 normally ends in -ed."},{"label":"Irregular verbs","title":"go → gone; see → seen; write → written","subtitle":"Check and learn the V3 forms of irregular verbs."}]}

{"title":"2. When we use Present Perfect","sections":[{"label":"Result now","color":"emerald","description":"Something happened in the past, and the result matters now.","examples":[{"en":"I have lost my wallet.","ua":"The result matters now."},{"en":"She has broken her glasses.","ua":"The situation is important now."}]},{"label":"Life experience","color":"blue","description":"Talk about experience in life without a finished past-time expression.","examples":[{"en":"We have been to Prague twice.","ua":"Life experience up to now."},{"en":"He has never ridden a horse.","ua":"No experience before now."}]},{"label":"Recent actions","color":"amber","description":"The action happened recently and still feels current.","examples":[{"en":"They have just arrived.","ua":"A very recent action."},{"en":"I have already sent the message.","ua":"The action is complete before now."}]},{"label":"Continuing situation or open period","color":"violet","description":"A state may still continue; completed actions are also possible when a period such as today or this week is still open.","examples":[{"en":"I have lived here for three years.","ua":"The situation continues now."},{"en":"She has had two meetings today.","ua":"Two meetings have taken place, but today is not over."}]}]}

{"title":"3. Quick form check","intro":"See how have / has combines with V3 and how the participle changes the meaning.","rows":[{"en":"I have finished my work.","ua":"have + finished","note":"I + have + V3"},{"en":"She has lost her keys.","ua":"has + lost","note":"she + has + V3"},{"en":"We have visited London.","ua":"have + visited","note":"we + have + V3"},{"en":"He has just arrived.","ua":"has + arrived","note":"he + has + V3"},{"en":"Anna has gone to the shop. / Anna has been to the shop.","ua":"Anna is still there or on the way / Anna visited and returned","note":"gone / been"}],"warning":"Do not say She have finished or I have went."}

{"title":"4. Common mistakes","items":[{"label":"Mistake 1","color":"rose","title":"Using V2 or V1 instead of V3.","wrong":"❌ I have went home.","right":"✅ I have gone home."},{"label":"Mistake 2","color":"amber","title":"Mixing up have and has.","wrong":"❌ She have finished the task.","right":"✅ She has finished the task."},{"label":"Mistake 3","color":"sky","title":"Using Present Perfect with a finished past-time expression.","wrong":"❌ I have seen him yesterday.","right":"✅ I saw him yesterday."}]}

{"title":"5. Short summary","items":["Present Perfect = have / has + V3; V3 is the verb's third form.","Use have with I / you / we / they and has with he / she / it.","Have / has is an auxiliary; contractions such as I've, she's, we've are natural in speech.","Use this tense for a result now, life experience, recent actions, and a period up to the present.","Do not combine Present Perfect with a finished past-time expression such as yesterday; since + starting point is correct.","Exercises with just / already follow British English and expect Present Perfect when the result matters now."]}

{"title":"6. Practice","select_title":"Exercise 1. Choose the correct form","select_intro":"Check have / has and the V3 form.","selects":[{"label":"a) She has finished the task. / b) She have finished the task.","prompt":"Which option is correct?","answer":"a"},{"label":"a) They have went home. / b) They have gone home.","prompt":"Which option is correct?","answer":"b"}],"options":["a","b"],"input_title":"Exercise 2. Build the sentence","input_intro":"Put the words in the correct order.","inputs":[{"before":"the report / finished / Tom / has","after":"→","answer":"Tom has finished the report."},{"before":"three emails / received / we / have","after":"→","answer":"We have received three emails."}]}
